policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: Qere הַיֹּשֶׁ֨בֶת֙ and ketiv הישבתי are the same feminine singular participle of ישב, the ketiv carrying only a paragogic yod; both render identically as a vocative address to Tyre. ASV 'O thou that dwellest at the entry of the sea' reflects that participle without any wording that would distinguish the two spellings, and the single ASV note on this verse is a hebrew_gloss ('Hebrew entrances') on מבואת, not a textual note mapped to this unit. Nothing in the English selects a reading.

Qere כִּתִּיִּֽים and ketiv כתים are plene and defective spellings of the same gentilic, Kittim. ASV 'from the isles of Kittim' transliterates the name and so cannot show which spelling stood before the translators. The verse's only note is classed alternative_rendering ('Or, deck'), which concerns the English rendering of the ivory benches and by policy never decides a reading.

Qere וְהָבְנִ֔ים and ketiv והובנים are defective and plene spellings of the same noun for ebony, differing only in the writing of the vowel. ASV 'horns of ivory and ebony' renders that noun once and identically under either spelling. The verse's only note is classed alternative_rendering ('Or, for a present'), which bears on the English of אשכרך and by policy never decides a reading.
